decision.reason: The piece uses get_tracer, start_as_current_span, set_attribute and record_exception; the crate is the same project's Rust API. Coverage of those four still has to be read against its documentation.

The piece only calls safe_load on a small config file. serde_yaml is marked deprecated by its author and serde_yml has an advisory; serde-saphyr is the maintained one. Its latest version is younger than the minimum publish age, so pin the one before it until that has passed.

The work is already done in compiled code inside scikit-learn, and the results of an isolation forest depend on its exact random-number use, which no other implementation reproduces. Port the code around it and call fit_predict across the boundary.

Crates with SOAP in the name exist; the figures in the report (age, releases, owners, use) do not describe anything to build a nightly job on. fetch_prices stays in Python and hands plain rows to the ported part.
